hints.title: Maximum Island Size Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the maximum area across all disconnected islands in an M x N grid requires ensuring that visited land cells are never counted more than once. How can in-place cell sinking sum each island area?

hints.title: Land Sink Invariant
hints.text: When a land cell (r, c) with value 1 is reached, sink it by setting grid[r][c] = 0 to prevent re-visitation while accumulating connected neighbors.

hints.title: Component Area Sinking Procedure
hints.text: Iterate across all cells (r, c). When grid[r][c] == 1, trigger a recursive helper: if out of bounds or grid[r][c] == 0, return 0. Set grid[r][c] = 0, return 1 + sum of helper calls across all 4 cardinal neighbors. Track the maximum returned area.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every cell is checked and converted to 0 at most once in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unmarked traversals result in exponential re-visitations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place grid cell mutation requires zero auxiliary visited matrix.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using in-place cell mutation to avoid extra visited matrix allocations.
